question: A triangular garden has vertices at coordinates A(2, 3), B(8, 11), and C(14, 7). A landscape designer wants to plant flowers covering exactly half of this triangular area. What area should be covered with flowers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use coordinate area shortcut:

Area = 1/2 | x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂) |

= 1/2 |2(11−7) + 8(7−3) + 14(3−11)|

= 1/2 |8 + 32 − 112| = 1/2 × 72 = 36

Half area = 18

**∴ Answer = 18 sq units**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Vertices A(2,3), B(8,11), C(14,7)

**Formula used:**

Area = 1/2 | x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂) |

 
 A(2,3) B(8,11) C

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 |2(11−7) + 8(7−3) + 14(3−11)|

⇒ = 1/2 |2×4 + 8×4 + 14×(−8)|

⇒ = 1/2 |8 + 32 − 112|

⇒ = 1/2 × 72

⇒ = 36 sq units

⇒ Required half area = 36 ÷ 2 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 sq units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Coordinate Geometry Area Formula

Area = 1/2 | x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂) |

Collinearity Check

If area = 0, points are collinear.

Geometric Meaning

Area represents the space enclosed by three non-collinear points.

Shortcut Tip

Always take absolute value to avoid negative area.
